target.title: add whatsapp outbound token diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can look successful when WhatsApp Web accepts a proactive 1:1 send but does not actually deliver it to a cold contact.

That is bad because the agent may believe a message was sent while the recipient never receives it. This PR makes that state easier to diagnose and avoids known PN/LID routing misses before send.

AI-assisted: yes, Codex helped update this branch and evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

WhatsApp/Baileys now stores and routes many direct contacts through LID JIDs. The old outbound path could trust stale local PN-to-LID files or miss the Baileys LID lookup path entirely.

This update keeps the fix local to the WhatsApp plugin:

- resolve phone-number targets through Baileys `getLIDForPN(...)` first
- fall back to a full-PN-JID USync lookup when needed
- refresh stale forward and reverse LID mapping files
- check trusted-contact token state for direct 1:1 sends
- keep token diagnostics best-effort during reconnect windows
- forward the needed socket query and diagnostic methods through the timeout adapter

## User Impact

Proactive WhatsApp sends should be less likely to go to a sender-only or wrong PN/LID target when Baileys already knows the contact LID.

When WhatsApp has an active reachout timelock and no trusted-contact token, OpenClaw now fails before `sendMessage` with a clearer error instead of letting the send look accepted but invisible.

If the socket is reconnecting, the new diagnostics do not block the existing send retry path.

## Evidence

Current head: `4bd3b8fd79cd745c7b243760e4504e3ab7365689`

Focused validation after rebasing on current `origin/main`:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-whatsapp.config.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/socket-timing.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       55 passed (55)
```

```text
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo
# exit code 0
```

```text
$ git diff --check
# exit code 0
```

```text
$ codex review --base origin/main
I did not find any discrete correctness, security, or maintainability issue introduced by the diff.
```

The focused tests cover:

- existing authDir PN-to-LID mapping is used for sendMessage
- Baileys `getLIDForPN(...)` is preferred before direct USync
- direct USync uses the full PN JID rather than only the phone value
- PN-JID recipients return the discovered LID directly
- stale local LID mappings are overwritten by the live lookup result
- active reachout timelock without trusted-contact token fails before sendMessage
- missing token diagnostics do not block when reachout timelock is inactive
- reconnect-window token lookup failures do not block the send retry path
- timeout adapter forwards the optional query and diagnostic socket methods

Not yet run: live WhatsApp delivery proof with a real account/contact.
